| --- | -------------- | ------------ | ----------- | -------- |
| 6   | 21/22 (95%)    | 0            | 5.5 s       | 6.5 s    |
| 8   | 20/22 (91%)    | 1            | 3.4 s       | 3.3 s    |

| Extra people          | 2                  |
| Errors                | 0                  |

- **Illegible marble:** the `"[]"` person from run 8 again. Also a parsing-layer fix.
- **Ellis 1818 → 1848:** the same worn-digit misread as every run.
- None of the three misses is a prompt problem. Run 10 stays in reserve.

- **Worn digits:** Ellis's 1818 was read as 1848 by every hosted model in run 1, and by Gemma 26B again in run 2. A zoomed crop confirms 1818. No model marked the digit with `?`.
- **Name formatting, not reading:** most name misses came with every date right.
  - "LE ROY" for LEROY (Flash both runs, 12B in run 2).
  - "LERØY" with a slashed O (Gemma 26B, run 2).
  - "M. ANDREW" for "Mr Andrew" (12B both runs, 26B in run 2).
  - Flash added the nickname "Eddie Boy" into Hildebrand III's name in run 2.
- **Gemma 31B's two run 2 errors were correct answers.** It followed valid JSON with a stray closing code fence. Both answers were right, including Ellis's 1818. Schema mode on the Gemini API doesn't stop it.
- **Gemma 26B listed a second person on Ellis** in run 2: "Thos. & Betsey Ellis", the parents named on the stone.
- **Local 12B invents surnames on worn stones:** "BETSEY BUCKS" (run 1) and "BETSEY BATES" (run 2) for Betsey Ellis. In run 2 it also returned a person named "[?]" for the illegible stone.
- **Local E2B is unusable:** without enforced JSON it echoed the schema's shape back. It read Ellis as "STIXIN George Davison", died 1878.

`holmquist-2024` was a companion stone: two first names over one shared surname. It was in run 1 and removed afterwards (multi-person stones are an MVP non-goal, see the PRD).

- Both Gemma models read every date correctly but returned "MARSHA FOX" and "CHARLES RAY", leaving off the shared HOLMQUIST.
- Gemini Flash got all 6 fields.
- Including it, run 1's hosted scores were Gemma 26B 75%, Gemma 31B 72% and Flash 86%. That gap is entirely this one stone.

- Gemma 4 matches Gemini Flash on single-person stones. The open model stays.
- Run 2 made hosted Gemma about 7–11× faster (26B: 24.5 s → 3.7 s). It is now faster than Flash.
- One call per image at temperature 1.0 is noisy: individual stones flipped between runs in both directions. Scores this close need repeated calls per image before they mean anything.
- Exact name strings are fragile across models. Normalization belongs in deterministic code, not the prompt.
- Even with an enforced schema, parse model output defensively: strip stray code fences before `JSON.parse`.
- Worn digits get misread confidently. A user-correction step is the fix; it is deferred to v2.
- Small local models (12B, E2B) guess on worn stones. Hosted Gemma it is.

Model choice is settled; from here the runs tune the prompt. Run 3 keeps run 2's prompt and schema ([`benchmarks/prompts/run3.json`](../../benchmarks/prompts/run3.json)) and only drops the temperature to 0.

| ------------------- | ------------------ |
| chambers-2011       | 3/3                |
| gonzalez-2021       | 3/3                |
| guo-2025            | 3/3                |
| hildebrand-iii-2018 | 3/3                |
| hildebrand-jr-2015  | 0/3                |
| cunningham-1752     | 0/3                |
| ellis-1818          | 0/3                |
| illegible-marble    | 0/1                |
| **Fields correct**  | **12/22 (55%)**    |
| Text similarity     | 97.7%              |
| Errors              | 0                  |

From run 4 on, every run is hosted `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` at temperature 0 with a system prompt and schema. Each run changes one thing from the run before it. The scorer now also counts **extra people**: entries for anyone the stone isn't for.

| 7   | `mediaResolution: MEDIA_RESOLUTION_LOW`                                          | 13/19 (68%)    | 2            | 11.5 s   | [`run7.json`](../../benchmarks/prompts/run7.json) | [`run7-hosted-26b.json`](../../benchmarks/results/run7-hosted-26b.json) |

- **Run 4:** the only field miss is Ellis's 1818 read as 1848. The extras were the nickname "Eddie Boy" listed as its own person, and Ellis's parents ("Thos. & Betsey Ellis").

- **Run 6 changed nothing.** 26B still reads 1848 with no `?`. Separate probes with thinking on (`thinkingLevel: HIGH`) and with `MEDIA_RESOLUTION_HIGH` also answered 1848.
- **Run 7 is a dead end.** A one-off probe at low resolution read 1818, but across all 8 stones it broke more than it fixed: Betsey Ellis came back named "\*years.\*", Hildebrand III returned broken JSON, and Cunningham picked up an extra person.

Run 6's slowdown was the free-tier queue, not the prompt. The same request re-sent right after run 6 took 2.8–4.8 s, the model spent no tokens thinking, and image size didn't change the model's input token count. The only lever the prompt controls is output length, so run 8 drops the full-inscription `text` field ([`run8.json`](../../benchmarks/prompts/run8.json), [`run8-hosted-26b.json`](../../benchmarks/results/run8-hosted-26b.json)). The scorer now reports median time, which a single queue spike can't drag.

| Run | Fields correct | Extra people | Median time | Avg time |
| --- | -------------- | ------------ | ----------- | -------- |
| 6   | 21/22 (95%)    | 0            | 5.5 s       | 6.5 s    |
| 8   | 20/22 (91%)    | 1            | 3.4 s       | 3.3 s    |

- Every named person read the same as in run 6.
- Regression: the illegible stone came back as a person literally named `"[]"`. A name with no letters is easy to reject in the deterministic parsing layer, so this is a code fix, not a prompt one.

## Run 9: the full 20-stone pool

The run 8 prompt, unchanged ([`run9.json`](../../benchmarks/prompts/run9.json)), on all 20 reviewed fixtures, now including 12 new single-person stones (9 deaths from 2010 on, 3 from 1993–2008). Raw output: [`run9-hosted-26b.json`](../../benchmarks/results/run9-hosted-26b.json).

| Metric                | gemma-4-26b-a4b-it |
| --------------------- | ------------------ |
| Fields correct        | 53/58 (91%)        |
| Extra people          | 2                  |
| Errors                | 0                  |
| Median time per photo | 4.1 s              |

- **Every date on every stone from 1950 on is right**, 14 stones in all, including VA bronze markers, a tarnished WWII plaque and a faint angled stone.
- **Hawks (0/3):** the dates were right, but the name came back as "Gaynor Claire Hawks née Staples". Stripping "née …" is a parsing-layer job, and the maiden name is worth keeping as a search signal.
- **Illegible marble:** the `"[]"` person from run 8 again. Also a parsing-layer fix.
- **Ellis 1818 → 1848:** the same worn-digit misread as every run.
- None of the three misses is a prompt problem. Run 10 stays in reserve.

## What went wrong

- **Worn digits:** Ellis's 1818 was read as 1848 by every hosted model in run 1, and by Gemma 26B again in run 2. A zoomed crop confirms 1818. No model marked the digit with `?`.
- **Name formatting, not reading:** most name misses came with every date right.
  - "LE ROY" for LEROY (Flash both runs, 12B in run 2).
  - "LERØY" with a slashed O (Gemma 26B, run 2).
  - "M. ANDREW" for "Mr Andrew" (12B both runs, 26B in run 2).
  - Flash added the nickname "Eddie Boy" into Hildebrand III's name in run 2.
- **Gemma 31B's two run 2 errors were correct answers.** It followed valid JSON with a stray closing code fence. Both answers were right, including Ellis's 1818. Schema mode on the Gemini API doesn't stop it.
- **Gemma 26B listed a second person on Ellis** in run 2: "Thos. & Betsey Ellis", the parents named on the stone.
- **Local 12B invents surnames on worn stones:** "BETSEY BUCKS" (run 1) and "BETSEY BATES" (run 2) for Betsey Ellis. In run 2 it also returned a person named "[?]" for the illegible stone.
- **Local E2B is unusable:** without enforced JSON it echoed the schema's shape back. It read Ellis as "STIXIN George Davison", died 1878.

## The dual stone that got cut

`holmquist-2024` was a companion stone: two first names over one shared surname. It was in run 1 and removed afterwards (multi-person stones are an MVP non-goal, see the PRD).

- Both Gemma models read every date correctly but returned "MARSHA FOX" and "CHARLES RAY", leaving off the shared HOLMQUIST.
- Gemini Flash got all 6 fields.
- Including it, run 1's hosted scores were Gemma 26B 75%, Gemma 31B 72% and Flash 86%. That gap is entirely this one stone.

## Takeaways

- Gemma 4 matches Gemini Flash on single-person stones. The open model stays.
- Run 2 made hosted Gemma about 7–11× faster (26B: 24.5 s → 3.7 s). It is now faster than Flash.
- One call per image at temperature 1.0 is noisy: individual stones flipped between runs in both directions. Scores this close need repeated calls per image before they mean anything.
- Exact name strings are fragile across models. Normalization belongs in deterministic code, not the prompt.
- Even with an enforced schema, parse model output defensively: strip stray code fences before `JSON.parse`.
- Worn digits get misread confidently. A user-correction step is the fix; it is deferred to v2.
- Small local models (12B, E2B) guess on worn stones. Hosted Gemma it is.

# Feature Specification: Gravespeaker MVP Journey

**Feature Branch**: `feat/mvp-journey`

**Created**: 2026-10-27

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "Gravespeaker MVP end-to-end journey per docs/PRD.md §2: capture/upload headstone photo, extract name + life dates via Gemma 4, search public records via SerpApi, verify identity (user picks candidate or none), generate source-grounded first-person narrative with per-sentence citations, show facts vs AI reconstruction. Use benchmarks/ results to inform decisions."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Read the stone (Priority: P1)

A visitor photographs a headstone on their phone (or picks an image on desktop) and sees the name and birth and death dates the app read from it.

**Why this priority**: Every later step depends on a correct reading. Alone, it already demonstrates the open model reading weathered stones.

**Independent Test**: Upload each reviewed fixture image and compare the displayed fields with `fixtures/manifest.json`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a phone browser, **When** the visitor chooses to photograph a stone, **Then** the device camera opens and the captured photo is submitted.
2. **Given** a desktop browser, **When** the visitor picks an image file, **Then** that image is submitted.
3. **Given** a legible single-person stone, **When** reading finishes, **Then** the name, birth date and death date are shown read-only before any search starts.
4. **Given** a stone with a worn digit the reader marked as unreadable, **When** fields are shown, **Then** the unreadable digit is shown as unknown, not guessed.
5. **Given** a stone with no legible name, **When** reading finishes, **Then** the app says no name could be read and offers to try another photo.
6. **Given** a name carved with a maiden name ("née Staples"), **When** fields are shown, **Then** the name is shown without the "née" clause and the maiden name is kept as a search signal.

---

### User Story 2 - Find and confirm the person (Priority: P2)

From the read fields, the app searches public records and shows candidate people, each with source links. The visitor picks the right person, or none.

**Why this priority**: Identity confirmation is the gate that stops misreads and namesakes from reaching the story.

**Independent Test**: With search responses recorded for a fixture, confirm candidates appear with source links and that picking "none" ends the journey without a story.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** extracted fields, **When** the search completes, **Then** each candidate shows name, life dates, place when known, and at least one source link.
2. **Given** results for two different people with the same name, **When** candidates are shown, **Then** they appear as separate candidates and are never combined.
3. **Given** exactly one plausible candidate, **When** results are shown, **Then** [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: Does a single match still require the visitor to confirm it, or does the story start automatically?]
4. **Given** candidates are shown, **When** the visitor picks "none of these", **Then** the app says no reliable record was found and no story is generated.
5. **Given** no records match, **When** search completes, **Then** the app says so plainly and no story is generated.

---

### User Story 3 - Hear their story (Priority: P3)

After confirming a person, the visitor reads a short first-person narrative in which every factual sentence links to its source, with documented facts visually distinct from AI reconstruction.

**Why this priority**: This is the payoff, but it is only trustworthy once Stories 1 and 2 hold.

**Independent Test**: For a confirmed candidate with recorded sources, every factual sentence in the narrative carries at least one citation that resolves to one of that candidate's sources.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a confirmed candidate, **When** the story is shown, **Then** it is labelled as an AI-generated historical reconstruction.
2. **Given** the story, **When** the visitor reads a factual sentence, **Then** it links to at least one source of the confirmed candidate.
3. **Given** the story, **When** displayed, **Then** documented facts and atmospheric reconstruction are visually distinct.
4. **Given** a source that names living relatives, **When** the story is generated, **Then** those relatives' names do not appear in it.
5. **Given** a generated sentence that states a fact no source supports, **When** the story is checked before display, **Then** that sentence is removed or the fact is rendered as unknown.
6. **Given** the confirmed candidate's records hold [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: What is the minimum evidence for a story — any record, or a record with content beyond the stone's own name and dates?], **When** the story would be generated, **Then** the app instead says there isn't enough on record to tell their story.

---

### Edge Cases

- Stone commemorates more than one person: [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: Multi-person stones are out of scope, but the reader may still return 2+ people. What happens?]
- Photo is not a headstone, or is blank: same outcome as "no legible name".
- Reader returns a "name" with no letters (`[]`, `[?]`): treated as no legible name (seen on the illegible fixture in runs 8 and 9).
- Reader output wrapped in stray code fences or otherwise malformed: parsed defensively; if still unusable, the visitor sees a retryable error.
- Only a birth or death year is carved, or a date is absent: shown as year-only or unknown; search still runs.
- Confident misread digit (Ellis 1818 → 1848): accepted in the MVP; it fails at the confirm step (no match or visitor picks none).
- Non-English inscription: not rejected; no special handling.
- Model or search provider fails or times out: visitor sees a plain error with a retry; no partial story is shown.
- Search result from a login-gated or paywalled source: not used as a candidate source.
- Image larger than the upload limit or not an image: rejected before reading with a clear message.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Visitors MUST be able to submit a headstone image from a phone camera or a desktop file picker.
- **FR-002**: System MUST reject non-image uploads and images over the size limit before reading.
- **FR-003**: System MUST extract, for the person the stone is for, the name and birth and death dates.
- **FR-004**: System MUST normalize extracted output in deterministic code: name cleanup (honorifics, "née" clause split into a maiden-name signal), date format (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY`, unknown digits), and rejection of letterless names.
- **FR-005**: System MUST show extracted fields read-only before searching.
- **FR-006**: System MUST search public obituaries, cemetery records and archives using name, dates and maiden name when present.
- **FR-007**: Every candidate MUST carry at least one source URL.
- **FR-008**: System MUST exclude login-gated and paywalled sources.
- **FR-009**: System MUST never combine records that may belong to different people into one candidate.
- **FR-010**: Visitors MUST be able to choose one candidate or "none of these".
- **FR-011**: System MUST generate a first-person narrative only from the confirmed candidate's sources.
- **FR-012**: Every factual sentence in the narrative MUST cite at least one of those sources; uncited factual claims MUST NOT be displayed.
- **FR-013**: Narrative MUST be labelled AI-generated and MUST visually separate documented facts from reconstruction.
- **FR-014**: Narrative MUST NOT name living relatives or other people mentioned in sources.
- **FR-015**: Narrative MUST NOT invent relationships, events, memories, thoughts or emotions.
- **FR-016**: When no credible record exists, the system MUST say so and MUST NOT generate a story.
- **FR-017**: Uploaded images MUST be processed in memory and never stored.
- **FR-018**: The browser MUST never call a model or search provider directly.
- **FR-019**: The journey MUST be usable on a phone-width screen.

### Key Entities

- **Extracted Inscription**: name as read, normalized name, maiden name (optional), birth date, death date; each date may be full, year-only, partially unknown, or absent.
- **Source Record**: URL, title, publisher/site, short snippet used for matching; never republished in full.
- **Candidate**: one hypothesized person — name, life dates, place when known, and the source records attributed to them.
- **Narrative**: ordered sentences; each sentence is either a cited fact (one or more Source Records) or labelled reconstruction.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: On the 20 reviewed fixtures, at least 55 of 58 fields are read correctly (run 9 scored 53/58; the Hawks "née" and illegible-stone misses are parsing fixes).
- **SC-002**: The illegible fixture yields "no legible name", never a person.
- **SC-003**: Median time from submitting a photo to seeing extracted fields is under 6 seconds (run 9 median: 4.1 s).
- **SC-004**: 100% of factual sentences in generated narratives cite a source belonging to the confirmed candidate.
- **SC-005**: Zero narratives are generated when the visitor picks "none" or no records are found.
- **SC-006**: A first-time visitor on a phone completes photo → story in under 2 minutes, excluding reading time.

## Assumptions

- Extraction uses hosted `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` with the run 9 prompt and schema, at temperature 0. It scored 91% on 20 stones at 4.1 s median and matched Gemini Flash on single-person stones; 31B is slower and emitted stray code fences.
- Narrative generation uses the same hosted Gemma 4 model unless the benchmark shows a grounding gap.
- Free-tier Gemini API latency spikes are tolerated; no paid tier.
- Field correction is a v2 feature; misreads fail at the confirm step.
- One person per stone; English inscriptions are the tuning target.
- No accounts, no persistence, no history between visits.
- Voice narration and other PRD Stretch items are out of scope.

4. **Given** a stone with a worn digit the reader marked as unreadable, **When** fields are shown, **Then** the unreadable digit is shown as unknown, not guessed.
5. **Given** a stone with no legible name, **When** reading finishes, **Then** the app says no name could be read and offers to try another photo.
6. **Given** a name carved with a maiden name ("née Staples"), **When** fields are shown, **Then** the name is shown without the "née" clause and the maiden name is kept as a search signal.

---

### User Story 2 - Find and confirm the person (Priority: P2)

From the read fields, the app searches public records and shows candidate people, each with source links. The visitor picks the right person, or none.

**Why this priority**: Identity confirmation is the gate that stops misreads and namesakes from reaching the story.

**Independent Test**: With search responses recorded for a fixture, confirm candidates appear with source links and that picking "none" ends the journey without a story.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** extracted fields, **When** the search completes, **Then** each candidate shows name, life dates, place when known, and at least one source link.
2. **Given** results for two different people with the same name, **When** candidates are shown, **Then** they appear as separate candidates and are never combined.
3. **Given** exactly one plausible candidate, **When** results are shown, **Then** the visitor must still confirm it or pick "none of these"; the story never starts automatically.
4. **Given** candidates are shown, **When** the visitor picks "none of these", **Then** the app says no reliable record was found and no story is generated.
5. **Given** no records match, **When** search completes, **Then** the app says so plainly and no story is generated.

---

### User Story 3 - Hear their story (Priority: P3)

After confirming a person, the visitor reads a short first-person narrative in which every factual sentence links to its source, with documented facts visually distinct from AI reconstruction.

**Why this priority**: This is the payoff, but it is only trustworthy once Stories 1 and 2 hold.

**Independent Test**: For a confirmed candidate with recorded sources, every factual sentence in the narrative carries at least one citation that resolves to one of that candidate's sources.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a confirmed candidate, **When** the story is shown, **Then** it is labelled as an AI-generated historical reconstruction.
2. **Given** the story, **When** the visitor reads a factual sentence, **Then** it links to at least one source of the confirmed candidate.
3. **Given** the story, **When** displayed, **Then** documented facts and atmospheric reconstruction are visually distinct.
4. **Given** a source that names living relatives, **When** the story is generated, **Then** those relatives' names do not appear in it.
5. **Given** a generated sentence that states a fact no source supports, **When** the story is checked before display, **Then** that sentence is removed or the fact is rendered as unknown.
6. **Given** the confirmed candidate's records hold nothing beyond what the stone already says (name and life dates only), **When** the story would be generated, **Then** the app instead says there isn't enough on record to tell their story.

---

### Edge Cases

- Stone commemorates more than one person: [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: Multi-person stones are out of scope, but the reader may still return 2+ people. What happens?]
- Photo is not a headstone, or is blank: same outcome as "no legible name".
- Reader returns a "name" with no letters (`[]`, `[?]`): treated as no legible name (seen on the illegible fixture in runs 8 and 9).
- Reader output wrapped in stray code fences or otherwise malformed: parsed defensively; if still unusable, the visitor sees a retryable error.
- Only a birth or death year is carved, or a date is absent: shown as year-only or unknown; search still runs.
- Confident misread digit (Ellis 1818 → 1848): accepted in the MVP; it fails at the confirm step (no match or visitor picks none).
- Non-English inscription: not rejected; no special handling.
- Model or search provider fails or times out: visitor sees a plain error with a retry; no partial story is shown.
- Search result from a login-gated or paywalled source: not used as a candidate source.
- Image larger than the upload limit or not an image: rejected before reading with a clear message.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Visitors MUST be able to submit a headstone image from a phone camera or a desktop file picker.
- **FR-002**: System MUST reject non-image uploads and images over the size limit before reading.
- **FR-003**: System MUST extract, for the person the stone is for, the name and birth and death dates.
- **FR-004**: System MUST normalize extracted output in deterministic code: name cleanup (honorifics, "née" clause split into a maiden-name signal), date format (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY`, unknown digits), and rejection of letterless names.
- **FR-005**: System MUST show extracted fields read-only before searching.
- **FR-006**: System MUST search public obituaries, cemetery records and archives using name, dates and maiden name when present.
- **FR-007**: Every candidate MUST carry at least one source URL.
- **FR-008**: System MUST exclude login-gated and paywalled sources.
- **FR-009**: System MUST never combine records that may belong to different people into one candidate.
- **FR-010**: Visitors MUST be able to choose one candidate or "none of these".
- **FR-011**: System MUST generate a first-person narrative only from the confirmed candidate's sources.
- **FR-012**: Every factual sentence in the narrative MUST cite at least one of those sources; uncited factual claims MUST NOT be displayed.
- **FR-013**: Narrative MUST be labelled AI-generated and MUST visually separate documented facts from reconstruction.
- **FR-014**: Narrative MUST NOT name living relatives or other people mentioned in sources.
- **FR-015**: Narrative MUST NOT invent relationships, events, memories, thoughts or emotions.
- **FR-016**: When no credible record exists, the system MUST say so and MUST NOT generate a story.
- **FR-017**: Uploaded images MUST be processed in memory and never stored.
- **FR-018**: The browser MUST never call a model or search provider directly.
- **FR-019**: The journey MUST be usable on a phone-width screen.

### Key Entities

- **Extracted Inscription**: name as read, normalized name, maiden name (optional), birth date, death date; each date may be full, year-only, partially unknown, or absent.
- **Source Record**: URL, title, publisher/site, short snippet used for matching; never republished in full.
- **Candidate**: one hypothesized person — name, life dates, place when known, and the source records attributed to them.
- **Narrative**: ordered sentences; each sentence is either a cited fact (one or more Source Records) or labelled reconstruction.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: On the 20 reviewed fixtures, at least 55 of 58 fields are read correctly (run 9 scored 53/58; the Hawks "née" and illegible-stone misses are parsing fixes).
- **SC-002**: The illegible fixture yields "no legible name", never a person.
- **SC-003**: Median time from submitting a photo to seeing extracted fields is under 6 seconds (run 9 median: 4.1 s).
- **SC-004**: 100% of factual sentences in generated narratives cite a source belonging to the confirmed candidate.
- **SC-005**: Zero narratives are generated when the visitor picks "none" or no records are found.
- **SC-006**: A first-time visitor on a phone completes photo → story in under 2 minutes, excluding reading time.

## Assumptions

- Extraction uses hosted `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` with the run 9 prompt and schema, at temperature 0. It scored 91% on 20 stones at 4.1 s median and matched Gemini Flash on single-person stones; 31B is slower and emitted stray code fences.
- Narrative generation uses the same hosted Gemma 4 model unless the benchmark shows a grounding gap.
- Free-tier Gemini API latency spikes are tolerated; no paid tier.
- Field correction is a v2 feature; misreads fail at the confirm step.
- One person per stone; English inscriptions are the tuning target.
- No accounts, no persistence, no history between visits.
- Voice narration and other PRD Stretch items are out of scope.

The spec is written and all 3 open questions are resolved. Nothing is committed yet.

**Branch:** `feat/mvp-journey`, created from a clean `main`.

## Files
- `specs/001-mvp-journey/spec.md`: 3 prioritized stories (read the stone → confirm the person → tell the story), 22 requirements, 10 edge cases and 6 success criteria.
- `specs/001-mvp-journey/checklists/requirements.md`: every quality check passes. Prettier is clean.
- `.specify/feature.json`: points later spec-kit steps at the new spec folder. It's gitignored, so it stays local.

## Your answers, now in the spec
- **One match found:** the visitor still has to confirm it (FR-011).
- **When to write a story:** only when a source says more than the stone's own name and dates. Otherwise the app says there isn't enough on record (FR-013).
- **More than one person on a stone:** each person read is shown read-only and the visitor picks one (FR-012).

## Decisions taken from the benchmarks
- **Reading model:** hosted `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` with the run 9 prompt at temperature 0. It scored 91% at 4.1 s median, matched Flash on single-person stones and had no code-fence breakage.
- **Fixes in the code layer, not the prompt:**
  - Reject names with no letters, which fixes the illegible stone coming back as a person named `"[]"`.
  - Split off "née …" and keep the maiden name as a search signal, which fixes Hawks.
  - Strip stray code fences before parsing.
- **SC-001:** at least 55/58 fields correct. That's run 9's 53/58 plus the two parsing fixes.
- **SC-003:** under 6 s median from photo to extracted fields.
- **Ellis 1818 → 1848:** the app accepts the misread. It fails at the confirm step, as the PRD allows.

## Assumption to check
- I assumed the story is also written by hosted Gemma 26B. If you'd rather benchmark Gemma against Flash on grounding before deciding, say so.

**Next:** `/speckit-plan`. Every question is already answered, so `/speckit-clarify` is optional.

 */

	const res = await fetch(
		`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/${model}:generateContent`,
		{
			method: 'POST',
			headers: {
				'content-type': 'application/json',
				'x-goog-api-key': process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY ?? ''
			},
			body: JSON.stringify({
				...(P.system && { systemInstruction: { parts: [{ text: P.system }] } }),
				contents: [
					{
						role: 'user',
						parts: [{ inline_data: { mime_type: 'image/jpeg', data: img } }, { text: P.user }]
					}

				generationConfig: {
					...P.sampling,
					...(P.mediaResolution && { mediaResolution: P.mediaResolution }),
					...(P.schema && { responseMimeType: 'application/json', responseJsonSchema: P.schema })
				}
			}),
			signal: AbortSignal.timeout(240_000)
		}
	);

	if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${res.status} ${body.error?.message ?? ''}`.slice(0, 200));

		.filter((p) => !p.thought)

}

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration

- No response from the browser extension

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.
