# HTTP Contract: Gravespeaker MVP

Three same-origin JSON endpoints. The browser calls only these; providers are server-side (FR-021). Entity shapes: [data-model.md](../data-model.md).

All errors: `{ "error": { "code": string, "message": string } }`, `message` safe to show the visitor.

| Code               | HTTP | When                                                 |
| ------------------ | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid_input`    | 400  | Body fails validation                                |
| `unsupported_type` | 415  | Upload is not an accepted image type                 |
| `too_large`        | 413  | Upload > 10 MB                                       |
| `provider_failed`  | 502  | Model or search failed after Mastra retries         |

## POST `/api/read`

Request: `multipart/form-data`, field `image` (jpeg/png/webp/heic/heif, ≤ 10 MB). Image bytes stay in memory for the request only.

Response 200:

```json
{ "people": [{ "carvedName": "GAYNOR CLAIRE HAWKS NÉE STAPLES", "name": "Gaynor Claire Hawks", "maidenName": "Staples", "born": "1941", "died": "2017-03-02" }] }
```

- `people: []` → no legible name (illegible stone, non-headstone photo).
- 2+ entries → client asks the visitor to pick one.

## POST `/api/research`

Request: one `Inscription` (as returned by `/api/read`).

Response 200:

```json
{ "candidates": [{ "name": "…", "born": "1941", "died": "2017", "place": "Leeds, England", "sources": [{ "id": "s1", "url": "https://…", "title": "…", "site": "…", "snippet": "…" }] }] }
```

- `candidates: []` → no record found.
- Gated domains already removed; no source appears in two candidates.

## POST `/api/story`

Request: `{ "inscription": Inscription, "candidate": Candidate }` — the candidate the visitor confirmed.

- Every `candidate.sources[].url` passes the SSRF guard (research R9) before fetch; failing URLs fall back to the snippet.

Response 200, one of:

```json
{ "status": "told", "sentences": [{ "text": "I was born in 1941.", "kind": "fact", "sourceIds": ["s1"] }, { "text": "The stone remembers me still.", "kind": "reconstruction", "sourceIds": [] }], "sources": [ … ] }
```

```json
{ "status": "insufficient" }
```

- `quote` and `claim` never appear in the response.
- Fetched page text never appears in the response.

# Implementation Plan: Gravespeaker MVP Journey

**Branch**: `feat/mvp-journey` | **Date**: 2026-10-27 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `specs/001-mvp-journey/spec.md`

## Summary

One SvelteKit page drives the journey photo → read → research → confirm → story. The page talks to three stateless JSON endpoints.

- Hosted Gemma 4 26B, called through Mastra Agents, reads the stone with the benchmark's run 9 prompt.
- SerpApi finds records.
- Gemma groups the results into candidates.
- After the visitor confirms a candidate, the server fetches that candidate's source pages in memory and Gemma writes a first-person story.
- Deterministic code owns the format and the grounding at every step:
  - name and date normalization;
  - identity merge and conflict rules;
  - citation and quote checks;
  - the evidence bar.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 6.0.x (strict, ESM) on Node 26.12.1

**Primary Dependencies**:

- Already in the repo: SvelteKit 3 with adapter-node, Svelte 5 runes.
- New:
  - `@mastra/core` (Agents, `createWorkflow`/`createStep`)
  - `zod` 4
  - `serpapi`
  - `@mozilla/readability`
  - `linkedom`
  - `robots-parser`

**Storage**: None. Images, fetched page text and journey state never persist.

**Testing**: Vitest unit tests with mocks at the Gemini and SerpApi boundaries, plus Playwright e2e on the page with mocked endpoints.

**Target Platform**: One Cloud Run service (Linux container). Mobile Safari, Chrome Android and desktop browsers.

**Project Type**: Web app, one SvelteKit project with UI and server endpoints.

**Performance Goals**: Median under 6 s from photo to fields (SC-003). Research and story each under about 20 s, bounded by the free-tier queue.

**Constraints**:

- Free Gemini API tier only.
- Upload limit 10 MB, with adapter-node `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=12M`.
- Page fetch: 8 s timeout, 2 MB cap, 5 pages at most.

**Scale/Scope**: Demo traffic. 1 page, 3 endpoints, and 8 server modules.

## Constitution Check

_Gate re-checked after Phase 1: **PASS**._

| Gate                       | Status | Evidence                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| I. Deadline-bound scope    | ✅     | Only PRD §2 steps. Voice, field editing and companion-stone tuning are excluded. The grounding benchmark is deferred to the next spec (R12). |
| II. Never fabricate        | ✅     | Each fact needs a valid `sourceId` and a quote found in that source (R8). The `insufficient` path exists. Unknown dates render as unknown. |
| III. Never merge silently  | ✅     | A source claimed by two candidates is removed from both. The visitor always confirms, even a single match (R7).                |
| IV. Two seams only         | ✅     | `InferenceProvider` (Gemma via Mastra) and `SearchProvider` (SerpApi), one implementation each. No cache, queue, flag or config layer. Retries are Mastra's. |
| V. Behavior-driven tests   | ✅     | The scenario table in [quickstart.md](quickstart.md) covers parsing, identity, grounding, validation and provider errors. Mocks sit only at Gemini and SerpApi. |
| Privacy                    | ✅     | Images stay in memory. Keys stay server-side. Page text is never returned. Living relatives are excluded by instruction. |
| Workflow                   | ✅     | One feature branch. `make ai-checks` is the gate.                                                                              |

## Project Structure

### Documentation (this feature)

```text
specs/001-mvp-journey/
├── plan.md
├── research.md
├── data-model.md
├── quickstart.md
├── contracts/api.md
└── tasks.md            # /speckit-tasks
```

### Source Code

```text
src/
├── routes/
│   ├── +page.svelte                 # journey state machine (data-model.md)
│   └── api/
│       ├── read/+server.ts          # upload checks → inference.readStone → inscription
│       ├── research/+server.ts      # research workflow
│       └── story/+server.ts         # story workflow
└── lib/
    ├── types.ts                     # Inscription, Candidate, SourceRecord, Story (shared with client)
    └── server/
        ├── env.ts                   # GEMINI_API_KEY, SERPAPI_API_KEY via $env/dynamic/private
        ├── inference/
        │   ├── index.ts             # InferenceProvider interface
        │   └── gemma.ts             # Mastra Agents: read, group, tell
        ├── search/
        │   ├── index.ts             # SearchProvider interface
        │   └── serpapi.ts
        ├── inscription.ts           # name/date normalization (R4)
        ├── identity.ts              # query build, gated filter, candidate rules (R5–R7)
        ├── pages.ts                 # SSRF-guarded fetch, robots, readability (R8–R9)
        ├── narrative.ts             # citation + quote validation, evidence bar (R8)
        ├── research.ts              # Mastra workflow: search (retries) → group → identity
        └── story.ts                 # Mastra workflow: fetch pages (retries) → tell → narrative
```

Tests sit next to each module as `*.test.ts`. The e2e test goes in `e2e/journey.test.ts`, following the repo's Playwright config.

**Structure Decision**: Keep the single SvelteKit project already in the repo. Server code lives in `src/lib/server/` per CLAUDE.md § Layout, and the two seam directories match the constitution.

## Deployment Notes

- Dockerfile: add `ENV BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=12M`. This edits repo config and is approved by this plan.
- `deploy.sh`: no change. It already maps `GRAVESPEAKER_GEMINI_API_KEY` and `GRAVESPEAKER_SERPAPI_API_KEY`.
- No new secrets.

## Complexity Tracking

No violations.

# Implementation Plan: Gravespeaker MVP Journey

**Branch**: `feat/mvp-journey` | **Date**: 2026-10-27 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `specs/001-mvp-journey/spec.md`

## Summary

One SvelteKit page drives the journey photo → read → research → confirm → story. The page talks to three stateless JSON endpoints.

- Hosted Gemma 4 26B, called through Mastra Agents, reads the stone with the benchmark's run 9 prompt.
- SerpApi finds records.
- Gemma groups the results into candidates.
- After the visitor confirms a candidate, the server fetches that candidate's source pages in memory and Gemma writes a first-person story.
- Deterministic code owns the format and the grounding at every step:
  - name and date normalization;
  - identity merge and conflict rules;
  - citation and quote checks;
  - the evidence bar.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 6.0.x (strict, ESM) on Node 26.12.1

**Primary Dependencies**:

- Already in the repo: SvelteKit 3 with adapter-node, Svelte 5 runes.
- New:
  - `@mastra/core` (Agents, `createWorkflow`/`createStep`)
  - `zod` 4
  - `serpapi`
  - `@mozilla/readability`
  - `linkedom`
  - `robots-parser`

**Storage**: None. Images, fetched page text and journey state never persist.

**Testing**: Vitest unit tests with mocks at the Gemini and SerpApi boundaries, plus Playwright e2e on the page with mocked endpoints.

**Target Platform**: One Cloud Run service (Linux container). Mobile Safari, Chrome Android and desktop browsers.

**Project Type**: Web app, one SvelteKit project with UI and server endpoints.

**Performance Goals**: Median under 6 s from photo to fields (SC-003). Research and story each under about 20 s, bounded by the free-tier queue.

**Constraints**:

- Free Gemini API tier only.
- Upload limit 10 MB, with adapter-node `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=12M`.
- Page fetch: 8 s timeout, 2 MB cap, 5 pages at most.

**Scale/Scope**: Demo traffic. 1 page, 3 endpoints, and 8 server modules.

## Constitution Check

_Gate re-checked after Phase 1: **PASS**._

| Gate                       | Status | Evidence                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| I. Deadline-bound scope    | ✅     | Only PRD §2 steps. Voice, field editing and companion-stone tuning are excluded. The grounding benchmark is deferred to the next spec (R12). |
| II. Never fabricate        | ✅     | Each fact needs a valid `sourceId` and a quote found in that source (R8). The `insufficient` path exists. Unknown dates render as unknown. |
| III. Never merge silently  | ✅     | A source claimed by two candidates is removed from both. The visitor always confirms, even a single match (R7).                |
| IV. Two seams only         | ✅     | `InferenceProvider` (Gemma via Mastra) and `SearchProvider` (SerpApi), one implementation each. No cache, queue, flag or config layer. Retries are Mastra's. |
| V. Behavior-driven tests   | ✅     | The scenario table in [quickstart.md](quickstart.md) covers parsing, identity, grounding, validation and provider errors. Mocks sit only at Gemini and SerpApi. |
| Privacy                    | ✅     | Images stay in memory. Keys stay server-side. Page text is never returned. Living relatives are excluded by instruction. |
| Workflow                   | ✅     | One feature branch. `make ai-checks` is the gate.                                                                              |

├── plan.md

│   ├── +page.svelte                 # journey state machine (data-model.md)
│   └── api/
│       ├── read/+server.ts          # upload checks → inference.readStone → inscription
│       ├── research/+server.ts      # research workflow
│       └── story/+server.ts         # story workflow
└── lib/

    └── server/
        ├── env.ts                   # GEMINI_API_KEY, SERPAPI_API_KEY via $env/dynamic/private

The plan is done and passes the constitution check before and after design. Nothing is committed; `specs/` is still untracked on `feat/mvp-journey`.

## Files
- `specs/001-mvp-journey/plan.md`: technical context, constitution gates, source layout and deploy notes.
- `research.md`: 12 decisions, each with the reason and what was rejected.
- `data-model.md`: the entities, their rules and a journey state diagram. Mermaid validated it.
- `contracts/api.md`: three endpoints (`/api/read`, `/api/research`, `/api/story`) and their error codes.
- `quickstart.md`: the test scenarios that must exist, the accuracy run against the fixtures, and phone and desktop walkthroughs.

## Decisions to know about
- **Stateless steps:** Mastra's pause-and-resume needs a database to save state. The spec rules out storage, so the server keeps nothing and the browser carries the journey from one request to the next.
- **Story grounding:** you chose fetching the source pages.
  - Each fact sentence must cite a source and carry a quote that appears in that source's text. Code drops any sentence that fails.
  - The quote and the page text never reach the browser.
- **Security:** the story request receives source URLs from the browser. Fetching them blindly on Cloud Run could reach the metadata server and leak the service account token.
  - Every fetch checks DNS and rejects private, loopback and link-local addresses, re-checking each redirect.
  - I chose this over signing the candidate list, which would need a new secret.
- **API key:** Mastra looks for `GOOGLE_API_KEY` by default. The plan passes `GEMINI_API_KEY` to it directly, so `deploy.sh` doesn't change.
- **Model and search retries:** Mastra's built-in retries only. No hand-rolled retry code.

## Approvals needed
- **New dependencies in `package.json`:** `@mastra/core`, `zod`, `serpapi`, `@mozilla/readability`, `linkedom`, `robots-parser`.
  - `@mastra/core` 1.79.0 was published today. If pnpm's release-age check rejects it, I pin the previous version.
- **Dockerfile:** raise `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT` from `10M` to `12M`. A 10 MB photo plus upload overhead would otherwise be rejected before the app's own size check.

## Deferred
- The PRD's Gemma-vs-Flash comparison of story grounding becomes the next spec. It needs this story pipeline to exist first.

**Next:** `/speckit-tasks`.

Sources:
- [Mastra Google provider (Gemma 4 model IDs, custom apiKey)](https://mastra.ai/models/providers/google)
- [Mastra createStep `retries`](https://mastra.ai/reference/workflows/step)
- [Mastra suspend/resume requires storage](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/main/docs/src/content/en/docs/workflows/suspend-and-resume.mdx)
- [SerpApi Google Search API](https://serpapi.com/search-api)
- [serpapi npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/serpapi)

> Heads up · Fetching full obituary pages also feeds the model their lists of living relatives, and only the story prompt keeps those names out.
>
> **Full obituaries bring living relatives' names**
> - You chose to have the server **read the full text** of source pages (obituaries, cemetery records), not just the short search previews.
> - Obituaries almost always list survivors by name, such as "survived by his wife Jane and son Mark."
> - The spec requires that the story **never names living relatives**.
> - Right now the only thing enforcing that is the instruction to the model. No code checks the finished story for those names.
> - **Consider asking for a code check, or a benchmark test on real obituaries,** that catches a relative's name before the story is shown.

I think that spec is overly harsh. It would be cool for the generated text to say something like "I left behind my wife of xx years. her name was y"

content.text:
This goes against the PRD as written, so I'm flagging it before changing anything.

- **PRD §4** says to leave out unnecessary sensitive details about living people, and its own example is "surviving relatives named in obituaries."
- **The constitution** repeats it: "Omit unnecessary details about living people."
- **Your example line names a survivor.** "Survived by his wife Jane" means Jane is alive. Most of the stones we test are from 2010 or later, so that's the usual case, not the rare one.
- **"Her name was y" would be wrong** when she's still alive. The model has no way to know otherwise.

The relationship itself is safe to keep, though. "I left behind my wife of 52 years" is a sourced fact and names nobody.

4. If no surviving fact has `claim: 'other'`, the response is `insufficient` (spec FR-013).
5. Fetched text is never returned to the browser or stored.

- **Rationale**: The user chose page text over snippets (2026-10-27). Snippets alone would fail the evidence bar on most stones. Quote matching gives a deterministic check against fabrication. The quote is never displayed, so source content isn't republished.

-- **Living relatives**: the agent instructions forbid naming anyone but the deceased. This is enforced by prompt and measured in the benchmark, not by code. Detecting names deterministically isn't reliable enough to ship.

+- **Relatives** (user decision, 2026-10-27): relationships are allowed as cited facts ("my wife of 52 years"). A relative may be named only when a cited source says they died first ("preceded in death by"). Survivors are never named. No code check: telling a survivor's name from a predeceased relative's takes reading comprehension, not a pattern.
- **Rejected**: Snippets only (user rejected); `jsdom`, which is heavier than `linkedom`; a headless browser, which is far too heavy.

---
description: 'Task list for the Gravespeaker MVP journey'
---

# Tasks: Gravespeaker MVP Journey

**Input**: `specs/001-mvp-journey/` — plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/api.md, quickstart.md

**Tests**: Required. `CLAUDE.md` § Tests mandates behavior tests for parsing, identity, grounding, input validation and provider errors. Mock only at the network boundary: stub `globalThis.fetch` for Gemini (`generativelanguage.googleapis.com`) and SerpApi (`serpapi.com`). Never hit live APIs in tests.

**Every task**: JSDoc on every function, method and class; inline comments only for _why_. Done = `make ai-checks` passes with zero warnings.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: parallelizable (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: US1 read the stone · US2 find and confirm · US3 tell the story

---

## Phase 1: Setup

- [ ] T001 Add exact-pinned runtime deps with `pnpm add --save-exact @mastra/core zod serpapi @mozilla/readability linkedom robots-parser` in `package.json`. If pnpm's release-age gate rejects a version, pin the previous release; never add `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` (research R11).
- [ ] T002 [P] Raise `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=10M` to `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=12M` in `Dockerfile` (research R10).

---

## Phase 2: Foundational

**⚠️ Blocks every story.**

- [ ] T003 [P] Create shared client/server types in `src/lib/types.ts`: `PartialDate` (string matching `^[0-9?]{4}(-[0-9?]{2}-[0-9?]{2})?$`), `Inscription { carvedName; name; maidenName: string | null; born: PartialDate | null; died: PartialDate | null }`, `SourceRecord { id; url; title; site; snippet }`, `Candidate { name; born; died; place: string | null; sources: SourceRecord[] }`, `StorySentence { text; kind: 'fact' | 'reconstruction'; sourceIds: string[] }`, `Story = { status: 'told'; sentences; sources } | { status: 'insufficient' }`, `ApiError { error: { code: 'invalid_input' | 'unsupported_type' | 'too_large' | 'provider_failed'; message } }`.
- [ ] T004 [P] Create `src/lib/server/env.ts` exporting `geminiApiKey()` and `serpApiKey()` read from `$env/dynamic/private` (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `SERPAPI_API_KEY`); throw a clear error when empty.
- [ ] T005 [P] Create `src/lib/server/http.ts`: `apiError(code, message, status)` returning a SvelteKit `json()` response in the `ApiError` shape, and `ProviderError` class thrown by both seams after Mastra retries are exhausted; endpoints map `ProviderError` → 502 `provider_failed`.
- [ ] T006 [P] Create the inference seam interface in `src/lib/server/inference/index.ts`: `InferenceProvider { readStone(image: Uint8Array, mimeType: string): Promise<RawPerson[]>; groupCandidates(inscription: Inscription, records: SourceRecord[]): Promise<RawCandidate[]>; tellStory(inscription: Inscription, candidate: Candidate, pages: PageText[]): Promise<RawSentence[]> }` with raw (pre-validation) types `RawPerson { name; born; died }`, `RawCandidate { name; born; died; place; resultIds: string[] }`, `RawSentence { text; kind; claim: 'name' | 'birth' | 'death' | 'other'; sourceIds: string[]; quote: string }`, `PageText { sourceId; text }`. One interface only.
- [ ] T007 [P] Create the search seam interface in `src/lib/server/search/index.ts`: `SearchProvider { search(query: string): Promise<SourceRecord[]> }`.
- [ ] T008 Create `src/lib/server/inference/gemma.ts` exporting `class GemmaProvider implements InferenceProvider` (methods filled per story) with one private factory building a Mastra `Agent` using `model: { id: 'google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it', apiKey: geminiApiKey() }` and Mastra `maxRetries` (research R3). Wrap a final provider failure in `ProviderError`. Export a module-level `inference` instance.

**Checkpoint**: seams and shared types exist.

---

## Phase 3: User Story 1 — Read the stone (P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: Photo → read-only name and life dates.

**Independent Test**: Upload each reviewed fixture; displayed fields match `fixtures/manifest.json` (quickstart § Extraction accuracy).

### Tests (write first, see them fail)

- [ ] T009 [P] [US1] `src/lib/server/inscription.test.ts`: `"[]"` and `"[?]"` names → person dropped; `"Gaynor Claire Hawks née Staples"` → `name "Gaynor Claire Hawks"`, `maidenName "Staples"`; `"nee"` without accent handled; `"Mr Andrew Morgan"` → honorific dropped; `"18?8"` kept; `"1932-03-10"` kept; `"March 1941"` → `null`; `"19"` → `null`; non-English letters (`"Ødegård"`) kept; empty array stays empty.
- [ ] T010 [P] [US1] `src/routes/api/read/server.test.ts`: `text/plain` upload → 415 `unsupported_type`; 11 MB jpeg → 413 `too_large`; missing `image` field → 400 `invalid_input`; stubbed Gemini reply for Hawks → 200 normalized person; stubbed Gemini reply wrapped in a ```` ```json ```` fence → still parsed (research R4 risk); stubbed Gemini 503 on every attempt → 502 `provider_failed`; reply `{"people":[{"name":"[]",…}]}` → `{ people: [] }`.

### Implementation

- [ ] T011 [US1] Implement `normalizeInscriptions(raw: RawPerson[]): Inscription[]` in `src/lib/server/inscription.ts`: drop names with no `\p{L}`; strip honorifics `Mr|Mrs|Miss|Dr` (case-insensitive, optional `.`); split `\b(née|nee)\s+(\S+)` into `maidenName`; collapse whitespace; keep `carvedName` as read; dates must match `^[0-9?]{4}(-[0-9?]{2}-[0-9?]{2})?$` else `null`.
- [ ] T012 [US1] Implement `GemmaProvider.readStone` in `src/lib/server/inference/gemma.ts`: system text imported from `benchmarks/prompts/run9.json` (single source of truth with the benchmark), user parts = image (`mimeType`) + run9 `user` text, `temperature: 0, topP: 0.95, topK: 64`, Mastra `structuredOutput` with a Zod schema mirroring run9's JSON schema. If T010's fenced-reply case fails, add a Mastra output processor — no hand parser.
- [ ] T013 [US1] Implement `POST` in `src/routes/api/read/+server.ts`: read `image` from `formData()`; accept only `image/jpeg|png|webp|heic|heif`; reject > 10 MB (`10 * 1024 * 1024`); bytes stay in memory; return `{ people: normalizeInscriptions(await inference.readStone(...)) }`.
- [ ] T014 [US1] Build capture + read UI in `src/routes/+page.svelte` (Svelte 5 runes, mobile-first): `<input type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment">`, states `Capture → Reading → (PickPerson | fields shown | no legible name)` per data-model state diagram; fields read-only; unknown dates rendered as "unknown" and `?` digits shown as-is; 2+ people → list to pick one (FR-012); "no legible name" offers retry; errors show `message` with retry.
- [ ] T015 [US1] Playwright e2e in `src/routes/journey.e2e.ts` with `page.route('/api/read', …)` mocks: single person shows read-only fields; `{ people: [] }` shows "no legible name" with retry; two people shows a picker. Run at a 390 px viewport.
- [ ] T016 [US1] Extraction accuracy run: copy `benchmarks/prompts/run9.json` to `benchmarks/prompts/run10.json`; make `benchmarks/run.ts` pass hosted replies through `normalizeInscriptions` and record `maidenName`; run `node benchmarks/run.ts benchmarks/prompts/run10.json benchmarks/results/run10-hosted-26b.json gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`; score with `benchmarks/score.ts`. Expected ≥ 55/58 fields, illegible fixture → no people, median < 6 s (SC-001–003). Append a "Run 10" section to `docs/benchmarks/ocr-smoke-test.md`. Never overwrite earlier runs.

**Checkpoint**: US1 deployable alone.

---

## Phase 4: User Story 2 — Find and confirm the person (P2)

**Goal**: Inscription → candidate people with sources → visitor picks one or none.

**Independent Test**: With stubbed SerpApi + Gemini replies, candidates show source links; "none of these" ends without a story.

### Tests (write first)

- [ ] T017 [P] [US2] `src/lib/server/identity.test.ts`:
  - `buildQuery`: full dates → `"Name" 1932 2017 (obituary OR grave OR cemetery)`; `18?8` year omitted; maiden name adds `OR "Gaynor Staples Hawks"`.
  - `dropGated`: `ancestry.com`, `www.newspapers.com`, `search.findmypast.co.uk` removed; `legacy.com`, `findagrave.com` kept.
  - `resolveCandidates`: unknown `resultId` dropped; a result claimed by two candidates removed from both; candidate left with no sources dropped; died year `2016` vs inscription `2017` dropped; inscription `18?8` matches `1818` and `1848`; null years never conflict; capped at 5 ordered by matched fields.
- [ ] T018 [P] [US2] `src/lib/server/search/serpapi.test.ts`: stubbed `organic_results` → `SourceRecord[]` with ids `s1…sN`, `site` = hostname; missing `organic_results` → `[]`; non-http link dropped; error body → `ProviderError` after retries.
- [ ] T019 [P] [US2] `src/routes/api/research/server.test.ts`: invalid body → 400; stubbed search with zero results → `{ candidates: [] }` without calling Gemini; stubbed search + grouping → candidates per contract; SerpApi failing every attempt → 502 `provider_failed`.

### Implementation

- [ ] T020 [P] [US2] Implement `class SerpApiProvider implements SearchProvider` in `src/lib/server/search/serpapi.ts` using `serpapi` `getJson('google', { q, num: 10, gl: 'us', hl: 'en', api_key })`. If the package does not call `globalThis.fetch` (breaking T018's boundary mock), call `https://serpapi.com/search.json` with `fetch` instead and remove the dependency. Export a module-level `search` instance.

- [ ] T032 [US3] Implement `GemmaProvider.tellStory` in `src/lib/server/inference/gemma.ts`. Instructions: first person as the deceased; every fact sentence cites `sourceIds` and copies a short verbatim `quote` from that source; reconstruction sentences are atmosphere only and add no facts; never invent relationships, events, memories, thoughts or emotions; relationships may be stated as cited facts; name a relative only when a cited source says they died before the deceased; never name survivors or other living people (FR-017). `structuredOutput` Zod schema `{ sentences: RawSentence[] }`; temperature 0.7.

The task list is ready: 39 tasks in `specs/001-mvp-journey/tasks.md`. All 39 follow the checklist format (checkbox, task ID, labels, file path). Nothing is committed yet.

## Breakdown
| Phase | Tasks | Run in parallel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Setup | T001–T002 | T002 |
| Foundational | T003–T008 | T003–T007 |
| US1: read the stone 🎯 MVP | T009–T016 (8) | T009, T010 |
| US2: find and confirm the person | T017–T026 (10) | T017–T021 |
| US3: tell the story | T027–T036 (10) | T027–T031 |
| Polish | T037–T039 | none |

19 tasks are marked as safe to run in parallel.

## How each story is tested on its own
- **US1:** upload each reviewed fixture photo. The fields shown must match the answer keys, at 55/58 or better.
- **US2:** with SerpApi and Gemini replies stubbed in tests, candidates show source links. "None of these" ends the journey without a story.
- **US3:** every fact sentence cites one of the confirmed candidate's sources. A story whose sources say no more than the stone returns `insufficient`.

## Decisions I made inside the tasks
- **Tests are included.** The spec doesn't ask for them, but your CLAUDE.md requires behavior tests. They're written before the code in every story.
- **The app imports its reading prompt from `benchmarks/prompts/run9.json` (T012).** The app and the benchmark can't drift apart that way.
- **Run 10 (T016)** passes the model's replies through the app's name and date clean-up before scoring. It writes new `run10` files and never overwrites earlier runs.
- **SerpApi (T020):** if the `serpapi` package doesn't use `fetch`, the tests can't fake its network calls. In that case it gets dropped and the code calls SerpApi's REST endpoint directly.
- **I corrected `quickstart.md`.** `make ai-checks` doesn't run e2e tests, so the page now lists `make e2e` separately.

## Suggested MVP
T001–T016: photo to read-only fields, deployed, plus the run 10 accuracy measurement. That lines up with the PRD's Wednesday milestone.

**Next:** `/speckit-analyze` for a consistency check across the spec, plan and tasks, or go straight to `/speckit-implement`.

| U2 | Underspecification | MEDIUM | research R8; tasks T031, T032 | The evidence bar (FR-013) trusts the model's `claim` label. A death-date quote labelled `other` passes the bar, so a story could be told from nothing but stone data. | In `groundStory`, don't count an `other` fact toward the bar when its quote contains only the name or date tokens. Add a test case to T028. |
| C1 | Constitution (V) | MEDIUM | tasks T019, T026 | "Without calling Gemini" and "never calls `/api/story`" check whether a mock was called. CLAUDE.md bans those tests. | Assert behavior instead. Make the Gemini stub throw, then assert `{ candidates: [] }` with status 200. In e2e, assert the no-record screen and that no story appears. |
| G2 | Coverage gap | MEDIUM | spec Edge Cases (provider fails); T025, T035 | Only the read screen (T014) handles errors with a retry. The research and story screens don't. | Add error and retry handling to T025 and T035, with e2e cases in T026 and T036. |
| I2 | Inconsistency | MEDIUM | tasks T016; CLAUDE.md § Benchmark | T016 changes `run.ts` to record normalized output. - SerpApi finds records.
- Gemma groups the results into candidates.

## R1. Reading model and prompt
-- **Decision**: Hosted `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` on the Gemini API, run 9 prompt and schema verbatim (`benchmarks/prompts/run9.json`), temperature 0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64, default media resolution.

## Constitution Check
Run the app's read path (model call + `inscription.ts` normalization) against all reviewed fixtures and score with `benchmarks/score.ts`. Save as the next `runN` files; never overwrite.
-Expected: ≥ 55/58 fields, illegible fixture returns no people, median < 6 s.
+Expected: ≥ 57/58 fields, illegible fixture returns no people, median < 6 s.
## Manual end-to-end (phone)
- Falls back to the search snippet when a fetch fails.
2. Sends the extracted text to the story agent, which returns sentences: `{ text, kind: 'fact' | 'reconstruction', claim: 'name' | 'birth' | 'death' | 'other', sourceIds[], quote }`.
3. Code keeps a `fact` sentence only if every `sourceId` belongs to the candidate and its `quote` appears, after normalization, in one cited source's text. Otherwise the sentence is dropped.
-  4. If no surviving fact has `claim: 'other'`, the response is `insufficient` (spec FR-013).

+  4. If no surviving fact has `claim: 'other'` with a quote containing a token beyond the deceased's name, month names and digits, the response is `insufficient` (spec FR-013). The model's `claim` label alone is never trusted for the bar.
5. Fetched text is never returned to the browser or stored.

- **Rationale**: The user chose page text over snippets (2026-10-27). Snippets alone would fail the evidence bar on most stones. Quote matching gives a deterministic check against fabrication. The quote is never displayed, so source content isn't republished.

- **Relatives** (user decision, 2026-10-27): relationships are allowed as cited facts ("my wife of 52 years"). A relative may be named only when a cited source says they died first ("preceded in death by"). Survivors are never named. The story agent's instructions enforce this, and the grounding benchmark (next spec) measures it with obituaries that list survivors. No code check: telling a survivor's name from a predeceased relative's takes reading comprehension, not a pattern.
- **Extracted Inscription**: name as read, normalized name, maiden name (optional), birth date, death date; each date may be full, year-only, partially unknown, or absent.
- **Source Record**: URL, title, publisher/site, short snippet used for matching; never republished in full.
- **Candidate**: one hypothesized person — name, life dates, place when known, and the source records attributed to them.
-- **Narrative**: ordered sentences; each sentence is either a cited fact (one or more Source Records) or labelled reconstruction.
+- **Story**: ordered sentences; each sentence is either a cited fact (one or more Source Records) or labelled reconstruction.
## Success Criteria _(mandatory)_
### Measurable Outcomes
-- **SC-001**: On the 20 reviewed fixtures, at least 55 of 58 fields are read correctly (run 9 scored 53/58; the Hawks "née" and illegible-stone misses are parsing fixes).

+- **SC-001**: On the 20 reviewed fixtures, at least 57 of 58 fields are read correctly (run 9 scored 53/58; the Hawks "née" fix recovers 3 fields and the illegible-stone fix 1; only the worn Ellis 1818 digit may still miss).
- **SC-002**: The illegible fixture yields "no legible name", never a person.
- **SC-003**: Median time from submitting a photo to seeing extracted fields is under 6 seconds (run 9 median: 4.1 s).
- **SC-004**: 100% of factual sentences in generated narratives cite a source belonging to the confirmed candidate.

content.text:
Good idea, with one conflict to settle before I touch the spec.

**The conflict: if "never display none" means removing the "None of these" button, that breaks Constitution III.**
- Constitution III and PRD step 4 both say the visitor picks one candidate or none.
- Without "none", a misread stone forces the visitor to pick a wrong person. Ellis 1818 read as 1848 is the case we already know about, and it would get a story about a stranger.

**What I'd build instead: keep the button, and send every dead end to a stone-only epitaph.**
- Those dead ends are: "none of these", no records found, and not enough on record.
- The epitaph is filled in by code from the fields read off the stone. No model call, so nothing can be invented:
  - "My name was Gaynor Claire Hawks."
  - "I was born on March 10, 1932, and I died on December 27, 2017."
  - "I've been here 9 years."
- Each line is left out when its field is unknown. A `?` digit drops the "years" line, so it never claims the wrong length of time.
- A short note under it still says no public records were found. The PRD requires the app to say so, and this keeps that.
- The stone is the cited source for every line.
- "No legible name" still asks for another photo, since there's no name to build on.

content.text:
The stone-only epitaph is now in the spec. Every path after a legible read ends on either an AI story or the epitaph. Nothing is committed. The diagram validates and Prettier passes.

**Example (Hawks, viewed 2026-10-31):**
> My name was Gaynor Claire Hawks. I was born on March 10, 1932. I died on December 27, 2017. I've been here 8 years.

**Rules:**
- Plain code builds it from the fields read off the stone. No model call.
- A sentence is left out when its field is unknown or has a `?` digit.
- A date with only a year reads "in 1932".
- The years line says "1 year" at exactly one year and "less than a year" under one.
- The headstone is the cited source, and the epitaph isn't labelled as AI-generated.
- A note under it explains why, depending on how the visitor got there:
  - "No public record was confirmed" after "none of these".
  - "No public records were found" when search finds nothing.
  - "The records hold nothing beyond the stone" when the evidence bar fails.

**What changed:**
- `spec.md`: new FR-023 for the epitaph. FR-013, FR-019 and SC-005 are reworded. Three test cases now end on the epitaph and two new ones cover the Hawks text and the `?` rule. There's also a new edge case.
- `data-model.md`: new Epitaph section, and the journey diagram's two dead-end states merge into one Epitaph state.
- `contracts/api.md`: an empty candidate list and `insufficient` both lead to the epitaph. No API change, because the browser builds it.
- `plan.md`: adds `src/lib/epitaph.ts` and updates the "never fabricate" gate to mention the epitaph.
- `quickstart.md`: epitaph test cases, and the Ellis walkthrough now ends on the epitaph.
- `tasks.md`: two new US2 tasks for the epitaph test (T019) and code (T020). Four existing UI and e2e tasks are reworded (now T026, T027, T037, T038). Tasks are renumbered and there are now 41.

**Known gap:** a misread date shows up in the epitaph, as with Ellis 1818 read as 1848. The PRD accepts misreads in the MVP, and the visitor already sees the read fields before searching.

**Next:** `/speckit-implement`.
